When US intelligence allegedly found a credible threat that Iran plotted to kill him last month, Trump left Air Force One in a catering truck, an episode first reported by the Washington Post and also by the New York Times. Trump downplayed the extraordinary nature of the subterfuge, as well as the risk to the people – White House officials, security and support staff, and reporters – he left on the plane, AP reported. “They wanted me to go on a different flight, different plane,” Trump told reporters after returning from an event in Ohio, saying he had little choice in the matter. “I guess there was a threat out there. https://www.luxurytravelmagazine.com/new.text: Home Page News Tourists Are Looking Beyond Daytime Sightseeing as Night Tours Boom Across Europe August 15, 2026 New search analysis reveals growing interest in night tours across major European cities, with Paris, Rome and London among the destinations seeing the strongest growth. Tourists are showing growing interest in exploring Europe’s busiest cities after dark, with night-tour searches increasing faster than searches for traditional day tours. A new search analysis from MyPrivateTours , a curated platform for instantly bookable private and semi-private tours, found that global searches for “night tours” reached an estimated 138,000 searches in June 2026, up 206% year-on-year. By comparison, “day tours” recorded an estimated 582,000 searches in June 2026, up 83% year-on-year. This means searches for night tours grew at around 2.5 times the rate of day tours over the same period. MyPrivateTours reviewed search demand across seven major European city destinations: Paris, Rome, London, Barcelona, Venice, Prague and Florence, with Paris, Rome and London showing some of the strongest growth in interest in night-time experiences. Key Findings Global searches for “night tours” reached an estimated 138,000 in June 2026, up 206% year-on-year. Searches for “day tours” reached an estimated 582,000, up 83% year-on-year. Night-tour searches therefore grew at around 2.5 times the rate of day-tour searches. Paris night-tour searches increased 1,691% year-on-year, compared with 137% for day tours. Rome night-tour searches increased 1,489% year-on-year, compared with 88% for day tours. London had the highest estimated night-tour search volume among the seven cities analysed, with approximately 6,000 searches in June 2026. Global searches for “night cruise” reached an estimated 446,000, up 148% year-on-year. Searches for “night food tours” increased 2,633% year-on-year. Searches for “Paris evening tour” increased 5,491% year-on-year. Paris Leads the Shift Towards Night Tours Paris showed one of the clearest differences between interest in day and night tours. Searches for “Paris night tours” increased 1,691% year-on-year, compared with a 137% increase for “Paris day tours.” This means Paris night-tour searches grew at more than 12 times the rate of day-tour searches year-on-year. The French capital offers a wide range of after-dark experiences, from illuminated landmarks and evening Seine cruises to food and cultural tours. Rome Is Seeing Rapid Growth in Night-Tour Interest Rome recorded the fastest growth in night-tour searches among the cities analysed. Searches for “Rome night tours” increased 1,489% year-on-year, compared with an 88% increase for “Rome day tours.” This means searches for Rome night tours grew at almost 17 times the rate of day-tour searches year-on-year. The trend highlights growing interest in experiencing Rome’s major landmarks and cultural attractions after dark. London Has the Highest Night-Tour Search Volume London recorded the highest estimated night-tour search volume among the seven cities analysed. In June 2026, searches for “London night tours” reached an estimated 6,000, compared with approximately 5,000 for Rome and 3,000 for Paris. London night-tour searches were also 590% higher year-on-year. The city’s combination of historic landmarks, evening river cruises, food experiences and illuminated attractions gives travellers a wide range of options for exploring after dark. Night Cruises and Food Tours Are Also Growing The increase in interest extends beyond traditional sightseeing tours. Global searches for “night cruise” reached an estimated 446,000 searches in June 2026, up 148% year-on-year. Searches for “night food tours” reached an estimated 7,000, up 2,633% year-on-year. Paris is also seeing increased interest in specific evening experiences. Searches for “evening Seine cruise” reached an estimated 3,000 searches in June 2026, up 1,259% year-on-year. Meanwhile, “Paris evening tour” recorded an estimated 2,000 searches, up 5,491% year-on-year. These figures suggest that growing interest in after-dark tourism extends beyond conventional sightseeing and into cruises, food and other evening experiences. Night Tourism Is Becoming a Bigger Part of the City-Break Experience The search data suggests that travellers are becoming more flexible about when they explore a destination. Rather than sightseeing being limited to daytime hours, evening experiences are becoming another way for visitors to experience major cities, landmarks and attractions. Night tours can offer a different atmosphere from daytime sightseeing, particularly for landmarks, river cruises, food tours and cultural experiences. Ahmed Tawfik, Co-Founder of MyPrivateTours, said, “Day tours are still a big part of city breaks, but travellers are becoming more flexible about when they choose to explore. “The strong growth in searches for evening and night tours shows that people are looking for different ways to experience major cities. “Night tours can offer a completely different atmosphere, whether that’s seeing landmarks after dark, taking an evening cruise or joining a food tour. “It’s not simply about taking the same tour later in the day. Travellers are looking for more varied, flexible and curated experiences.” Methodology The analysis used estimated search-demand data from Google Trends and Glimpse, which converts Google Trends data into estimated search volumes. MyPrivateTours reviewed search demand across seven major European city destinations: Paris, Rome, London, Barcelona, Venice, Prague and Florence, comparing search interest for night tours with day tours. The analysis examined June 2026 search volumes and year-on-year changes to identify longer-term changes in interest. Additional searches relating to night cruises, food tours and evening experiences were also reviewed. All search-volume figures are estimates derived from Glimpse’s conversion of Google Trends data and should be treated as indicative rather than exact search counts. A manual review of Tripadvisor listings was conducted to provide additional context around the availability and types of bookable evening experiences in selected cities. Because Tripadvisor listings are dynamic, these findings represent a snapshot at the time of research and are not intended to provide a permanent market ranking. All data was collected and analysed in July 2026, using June 2026 as the latest complete month of search data. About MyPrivateTours MyPrivateTours is a curated platform for instantly bookable private and semi-private tours. The platform helps travellers find higher-quality experiences with smarter timing, particularly when visiting major cities, landmarks and cultural attractions. MyPrivateTours focuses on more personal and flexible ways to explore popular destinations. Photograph: George Sweeney/Alamy View image in fullscreen Omar Barghouti said international law requires the UK to end all trade, diplomatic and economic relations with Israel. Photograph: George Sweeney/Alamy Israel UK must end all trade with Israel, says co-founder of BDS movement Exclusive: sanctions against ministers and settler groups are ‘smoke and mirrors cop-out’ says Omar Barghouti Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor Wed 2 Sep 2026 02.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 02.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Britain’s legal and ethical obligation to stop a genocide in Gaza requires it to take bigger steps than halting trade with illegal Israeli settlements or imposing further sanctions, Omar Barghouti, the co-founder of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement has said. He described sanctions against individual settler groups or extremist ministers as a “smoke and mirrors cop-out and distraction” from the UK’s legal obligation under international law to end all support for Israel, including arms exports, trade deals and academic relations that “may directly or indirectly enable Israel’s illegal occupation” of Gaza, the West Bank and East Jerusalem. The British foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, promised on Tuesday to introduce a “comprehensive reset” of the UK’s policy on Israel in the coming weeks. It has been reported that the UK is preparing to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank and Miliband told the Commons the government was looking at how to stop British companies “financing, constructing or advertising new settlements”. Ed Miliband promises ‘comprehensive reset’ of UK policy toward Israel Read more Miliband has called plans for the E1 settlement , which would involve the construction of 3,400 houses through the heart of the West Bank, unacceptable and destructive, adding that, by cutting across the territory, critics say it will render a two-state solution impossible. Tenders for the settlements are due to be handed out, potentially irreversibly, days before the Israeli elections on 27 October. The Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council have warned Miliband that a UK ban on trade with settlements may fuel antisemitism in the UK. A third group of British Jews, Yachad, also met Miliband to highlight “the growing concerns of many British Jews about the entrenchment of occupation and effective annexation of the West Bank”. Barghouti, an influential advocate for Palestinian rights for more than 20 years, said the litmus test for human rights law and the west still lay in Palestine. He said: “In July 2024, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said Israel’s entire occupation of Gaza, and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is illegal and amounts to a violation of the racial segregation and apartheid prohibitions under international law. “Dozens of UN human rights experts have said to fulfil those obligations a set of minimal steps are required: a full military embargo, export import, dual-use transfer and transit. “They also said you have to end all trade, diplomatic and economic relations and academic relations that enable Israel’s illegal occupation.” Barghouti added: “Further in January 2024, the ICJ said there is a plausible case of the violation of Palestinian rights under the Genocide Convention. “The ICJ decided there is a plausible risk of genocide that is sufficient to trigger third state responsibilities. But UK government lawyers seem to ignore that part of the ruling and say the court has not ruled on genocide. “But the genocide convention is very clear – where there is a risk, the obligation to prevent is triggered, and how do you prevent a genocide? You stop enabling it. You end all forms of complicity.” The Israeli embassy referred to the warning by Gideon Sa’ar, Israel’s foreign minister, who said: “If Britain acts against the state of Israel, the state of Israel will act against Britain. We have the tools.” He added: “The period is over when people act against the state of Israel and the state of Israel doesn’t respond.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines UK Get the day’s headlines and highlights emailed direct to you every morning after newsletter promotion Burnham to face pressure at Labour conference to recognise Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide Read more Explaining why he regards UK sanctions as “totally performative”, Barghouti said: “They have no concrete effect in holding Israel to account or pressuring it to comply with international law.” He added: “Israel has de facto annexed the occupied Palestinian territory, making it near impossible [to] differentiate so-called settlement goods and services.” Pressed whether the BDS movement is trying to change the minds of Israelis through economic force, Barghouti insisted sanctions have to be legal and ethical. “They have to target the perpetrators, whether entities or individuals that are involved in crimes, especially international crimes. They are actually measures of accountability, not sanctions that simply say settlers shall not have vacations in London.” Despite South Africa feeling forced to return to the ICJ to point out Israel is not complying with court orders, he said he retained his faith in international law – for all its colonial origins – arguing it was not something engraved in stone, but dynamic. “Humanity has agency to evolve and expand international law. We in the BDS movement have been pushing the envelope of its interpretation.” Barghouti added: “So, in the BDS movement, we try to hold states, corporations and institutions accountable to end their own complicity in genocide rather than just wait for the messiah of international law to come and save us. “We definitely need international law, just as we need to maintain the ethical high ground. Both are necessary, but not sufficient. We need people power to achieve liberation. https://www.hexham-courant.co.uk/news/26.text: Events Leisure Ovington Village Fete brings community together again By Sonia Veneziani-Rocha Reporter Share 0 Comments 14 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Homemade cakes, classic games and community spirit were in full supply at this year’s Ovington Village Fete. Held on Saturday, September 5, the annual event in the Tyne Valley drew crowds with its mix of traditional fun and family-friendly activities, all organised by the Ovington Community Group. Visitors enjoyed games including tin can alley and splat the rat, alongside stalls offering everything from body care products and second-hand books to bric-a-brac and plants. Vintage cars were on display, and the ever-popular tea tent served up homemade cakes and pastries. Magician Paul Innes entertained the crowd with walkabout performances filled with comedy and sleight of hand. Phil Lloyd, a village stallholder, raised more than £300 for his son Gethin’s Prudhoe Scout World Jamboree trip to Poland by selling handmade pottery. Children kept busy throughout the afternoon by making and chasing giant bubbles, hula-hooping, and playing with diablos and flower sticks, while some queued up to show off their acrobatic skills on crash mats laid out on the green. The North East Rock Choir, led by Rob Slater, performed well-known rock hits and brought what organisers described as "joyous singing" and "feelings of wellbeing and friendship" to the event. The choir is made up of members from across the region, including several from Ovington itself. Compere Lisa Leggatt later drew the raffle, and The Ovington Leek Club auctioned off several giant vegetables. The event closed with cheers for the village and its organisers. Mr Lloyd’s stall proved especially popular, featuring turquoise crackle glaze mugs bearing the Ovington insignia. The Ovington Village Fete remains a highlight of the Tyne Valley calendar, celebrating community spirit and simple pleasures.
